title: A Friend From Middle School
text: “Huh? Beep-beep.”

When I returned to the carriage via the portal, the Lazy Pig—who’d been reading with a total lack of enthusiasm—looked up and called out to me. This guy’s always lying down, no matter when I see him. I’m seriously considering just roasting him whole.
“I’m back. Did anything weird happen?”
Yuki-chan answered Father’s question.
“There were no particular problems. This person didn’t act strangely either. It’s just… I couldn’t sense even a shred of motivation from him.”
“Boo-boo.”
“Ahaha… Well, as long as nothing major happened, that’s good. There weren’t any bandit attacks or anything, were there?”
“No.”
“I suppose we can safely assume they aren’t on high alert just yet? Looks like Motoyasu-kun’s strategy has paid off.”
“Those are kind words!”
“For now… let’s keep peddling like this while leveling up and strengthening our characters behind the scenes. That way, we’ll steadily get stronger. Of course, we can’t let our guard down.”

That’s right. As Father instructed, we should focus on boosting Yuki-chan and the others’ levels tomorrow. As a result, Sakura-chan, Father, Keel, and Pig will all level up as well. Let’s aim for Class Up.

The problem is that the great Filolial-sama won’t grant us special Class Up assistance. It’d be great if we could run into them somewhere… but it’s hard to recreate the circumstances that led to our previous encounter with the Filolial-sama. The first time I met them was when I was crossing a mountain pass with Ku and the others. Do you think we’d run into them if we ran around that area? I have a feeling it’ll be pretty tough.

The next place we’re likely to run into them is… on the road to Siltvelt… It’s fine to go looking for them, but considering I have to return to the portal regularly, it’ll still be a hassle to run into them. Well… I seem to recall my future Father mentioning the time he met a large Filolial-sama.

That was when Filo-tan became dramatically stronger… I believe it was around the time my Father was officially placed on the wanted list, when he was in hiding in Melromarc with his Finacée. If that’s the case, it’s still quite a ways off. Well… the Class Up bonuses are excellent, but they’re not so great that you can’t make up for it with attribute improvements. Worst-case scenario, if you just reset your level, we can handle it either way.

Attribute enhancements themselves remain even after a reset, so if you’ve been defeating powerful monsters around Level 40, that’s a range a hero can easily reach. And so, our leveling process proceeded without a hitch.

My Father has decreed that we can only use the money earned from peddling in Melromarc, so we’re keeping the loot collected in Siltvelt unused. However, the weapons used by Keel and Sakura-chan are a different story. They affect our hunting efficiency. Still, since swinging around unfamiliar weapons would arouse suspicion, we’re limiting their use to Siltvelt as well.

About a week of days like that passed. During that time, Father continued to travel around selling medicine, using his shield skills. For those with severe illnesses or deep wounds, he would pull his robe tightly over his face so his identity wouldn’t be revealed, then administer the medicine. I also assisted with the treatments as his partner.

Lately, word of mouth has led people to call our carriage “the carriage that spreads the miracles of the Divine Bird.” When we arrive in a town, people even come out, bowing their heads or praying, asking to be treated. Father responds with a smile and treats them as best he can. We generally accept payment, but sometimes he’ll treat the poor for free.

Well, since we’ve only been traveling as peddlers for nearly two weeks, we’ve only covered a very small portion of the region so far. There isn’t enough time to travel all over Melromarc. Well, since we have two whole months, we’ll just have to make our rounds during that time.
“It’s been almost three weeks since we were summoned, hasn’t it?”
“That’s right. There’s only one week left until the first wave.”
“Looks like it. We’re steadily gathering money, but… it’s about time we started thinking about other businesses besides medicine. We’re not really turning a profit.”

After all, my Father is a kind man. He sells medicine at low prices and even provides treatment on top of that. I hear the number of patients coming to my Father—desperate for money and clinging to any last straw—is on the rise. So, my Father has been putting off payments more and more often, telling them, “It’s fine to pay later… whenever you have the means.”

“I know that, given our situation, we should be collecting money like misers, right? It’s just… you know? When I think about how much money there is in Siltvelt, I naturally end up being too lenient… “I’m sorry, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Don’t worry about it.”

Even in his original world, my Father was known as the “Saint of the Divine Bird.” I’m sure my Father from the future was doing something similar as well. When my Father ended up being chased by us, the reason people tried to help him and his group escape was likely because of the goodwill he’d built up in this way. If you think of it as the necessary cost for that, it’s a small price to pay.
“The problem is Class Up, isn’t it?”
“Yeah… We’ve been getting by by faking it with aptitude improvements, but I think it’s about time we actually did it.”
“Boo-boo!”
“Yeah. According to Motoyasu-kun, once Keel-kun Class Ups, he’ll be able to transform into a beast, so we should definitely do it.”
“Boo!”
Keel is leaning forward, looking pretty excited. Do you really want to do a Class Up that badly?
“I’ve been thinking it’s about time I went over to Siltvelt to talk things out, so shall we go? What about you, Elena?”
“Boo…”
“Huh? Since there’s probably some tedious paperwork involved, should you wait in the carriage this time?”
The pig nodded. Just how much of a slacker is he, anyway? Well, fine. We’ll need to keep a low profile either way, after all.

Perhaps the Three Heroes Church cultists disguised as bandits realized that a careless ambush would result in their equipment being seized—which would only strengthen Father’s faction—because they haven’t been showing up much lately. Instead, rumors are swirling about criminals in various regions claiming to be the Shield Hero. I also heard this rumor… shortly before heading out for the second wave.
But their disguises are pointless. My father isn’t famous as the Shield Hero these days. Instead, he’s becoming famous as the Saint of the Divine Bird while keeping a low profile.

Anyway, after the first wave, when I had some free time, I took the Crimson Swine to Zeltoble to stock up on gear. Though I did get kicked by Filo-tan a few times before that. Those days feel like a distant memory now.

Filo-tan… That’s right. Lately, when I have free time, I’ve been passing the time by drawing pictures of Filo-tan, which I’d put on hold. I have plenty of time while waiting in the carriage, after all.
“Motoyasu-kun? Are you drawing again?”
“That’s right. Are you ready yet?”
“Ah, yeah.”
My Father takes a look at the picture of Filo-tan I drew.
“That’s good. Is this the girl Motoyasu-kun likes?”
“That’s right.”
“The drawing of her in her Filolial form looks a bit like Sakura-chan… but the color scheme is different.”
“That’s right. She does look somewhat similar to Sakura-chan.”
“Hmm? What about Sakura?”
Sakura-chan comes over to look at the drawing I made.
“Motoyasu-kun says the girl he likes has a color scheme similar to Sakura-chan’s.”
“Is that so? Hmm.”
“This is her angel form.”
“It’s black and white, but yeah. She looks like a character I’ve seen in video games or something. I think she’s a sweet, innocent-looking girl.”
Ah, Filo-tan… Where are you right now?
“Hmm?”
Sakura-chan is tilting her head as she looks at the picture of Filo-tan I drew.
“Apparently, I’m this girl’s owner.”
“Naofumi, is this how you wanted Sakura to turn out?”
Sakura-chan is asking her Father. Haha, what a heartwarming sight.
“No, no. I just thought she was a girl every bit as lovely as Sakura-chan.”
“Do you like girls, Naofumi?”
“Well, I like them as much as anyone else. But right now, I’ve got things I need to do that are more important than romance.”
“Is Sakura cute?”
“Cute, cute.”
“Boo!”
“That’s right. Sakura-chan is a real beauty. Keel-kun, do your best not to be outdone.”
“Buh!? Buh-buh-buh!”
“Ahaha, sorry, sorry. I forgot Keel-kun is a boy.”
Ignoring the Fathers’ lighthearted banter, Yuki-chan is looking at the picture of Filo-tan I drew. What do you think? She looks magnificent, doesn’t she?
“Is this the girl Motoyasu-sama has his eye on in the future?”
“Looks like it. Oh, Yuki-chan, are you jealous by any chance?”
“No, I’m not!”
Yuki-chan is shaking her head vigorously from side to side. Father is watching her with a cheerful expression.
“Really?”
“I just want to be of help to Lord Motoyasu.”
“Is that so? I was totally convinced you liked Motoyasu-kun.”
And for some reason, Father shot me a deliberately exaggerated glance. It’s a reaction similar to that of a guy who befriended me back in middle school.

He was a guy who knew an oddly detailed amount about pigs. Strangely enough, we got along well, and we used to talk a lot. To begin with, I was the type who had extremely few male friends, so aside from him, I hardly had any other male friends.

That guy, though—he was trying to foist his interest in pigs onto me. He was well-versed in pig-related hobbies and behaviors, and even had photos and such. Well, when we went on to high school, we ended up at different schools and stopped seeing each other. Looking back, he was a rare kind of guy.

If he wanted a pig that badly, why didn’t he just use that information to approach one himself? Thinking about it now, he really was a strange guy. But strangely enough, I didn’t feel any aversion toward him.

I don’t know anyone to whom the word “meticulous” fits as well as it did to that guy. Even though he was so knowledgeable about pigs, he himself had absolutely no interaction with them whatsoever. He was the kind of guy who seemed to be gathering information just to push pigs onto me.
“As I’ve said before, Father, you have a great sense of humor. To me, Filolial-sama is like my own child.”
“Huh?”
“Every child is a precious child. It’s not as if I’d ever fall in love with or marry a child, is it? The only one I long for is Filo-tan.”
“Ah… yeah. Yuki-chan, good luck.”
“I told you, I don’t have those kinds of feelings!”
My Father is soothing Yuki-chan, who’s huffing and puffing in a huff.
“Well then, Motoyasu-kun, shall we head out?”
“Understood.”
We activated the Portal Spear and traveled to Siltvelt.
